LESSON: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON-FICTION MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we read non-fiction materials?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read
2. read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON-FICTION MATERIALS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON-FICTION MATERIALS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read

What this means
In this part you learn to identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials to a partner. (skill: read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read.
3. Practise this skill: read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read non-fiction materials?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non-Fiction materials means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify print or electronic non- fiction materials that are interesting to read.
5. Be able to: read a variety of grade- appropriate non-fiction materials independently for lifelong learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
